Generate a manhattan plot one or more mechGEA outputs.

plot_manhattan.Rd

Creates a ggplot-based manhattan plot, where chromosomes/scaffolds/etc are concatenated along the x-axis. Works with mechGEA SNP_pvalue outputs; take either a single output or a list of outputs from multiple chunks (see details).

Usage

plot_manhattan(
  SNP_pvalues,
  SNP_metadata,
  vlines = FALSE,
  vline_width = 0.25,
  significant = 5,
  suggestive = 3,
  colors = c("black", "slategray3"),
  chr_order = NULL,
  abbreviate_labels = FALSE,
  env_colors = NULL
)

Arguments

SNP_pvalues

data.frame or similar like that produced by mechGEA in $SNP_pvalues OR the output from mechGEA \ run_stan_GEA_model OR a list of a either of the two (mixing OK). If the former, contains three columns named "SNP", "Env", and "nlogp" containing SNP IDs, names for environmental effects, and -log p-values for associations.

SNP_metadata

data.frame or similar containing metadata on SNPs OR a path to a ".beagle" or ".beagle.gz" file containing SNP metadata OR a list of a either of the two (mixing OK). If the former, must have three columns named "SNP", "CHROM", and "POS" containing SNP IDs, chromosomes, and positions for each SNP. Each SNP ID in the SNP_pvalues "SNP" column must be represented in the "SNP" column of SNP_metadata. Assumes sorting is in the same order as in SNP_pvalues, across lists or not.

vlines

character (color) or FALSE, default FALSE. If a color, vertical separator lines will be drawn between each chromosome. Widths controlled by vline_width.

vline_width

numeric, default 2. Width of chromosome separator lines. Ignored if vlines is FALSE.

significant

numeric, default NULL. Value at which a line will be drawn designating significant SNPs. If highlight = "significant", SNPs above this level will also be labeled.

suggestive

numeric, default NULL. Value at which a line will be drawn designating suggestive SNPs. If highlight = "suggestive", SNPs above this level will also be labeled.

colors

character, default c("black", "slategray3"). Colors to alternate across chromosomes.

chr_order

character, default NULL. If provided, an ordered vector of chromosome/scaffold/etc names by which to sort output.

abbreviate_labels

numeric or FALSE, default FALSE. If a numeric value, x-axis chromosome names will be abbreviated using abbreviate, with each abbreviated label having the minimum length specified. Helpful when chromosome/scaffold/etc names are very long.

env_colors

character, default NULL. An optional vector of colors to use for each environmental variable.

Author

William Hemstrom

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# run a model
beagle <- system.file("extdata", "example.beagle.gz", package = "mechGEA")
phred <- beagle2pl(beagle, lines = 1:150)
input_data <- prepare_metadata(sample_metadata)
res <- mechGEA(phred,
               patch_info = input_data$patch_info,
               patches_xy = input_data$patches_xy,
               migration_loci = 50,
               env = input_data$env,
               iter_sampling_gea = 100,
               iter_warmup_gea = 200,
               iter_sampling_mig = 100,
               iter_warmup_mig = 200)

# plot results
plot_manhattan(res, beagle)
## or
plot_manhattan(res$SNP_pvalues, beagle)
# or could provide a data.frame of SNP metadata


# combine across result runs. Note that using chunk_beagle() is easier, than
# manually splitting, but for the example we're just making two chunks
beagle <- system.file("extdata", "example.beagle.gz", package = "mechGEA")
system(paste0("zcat ", beagle2,
              " | head -n ", 301, " | gzip > test_sub.beagle.gz"))
b <- fread(" test_sub.beagle.gz")
b <- b[151:300,] # the second batch of lines
fwrite(b, "test_sub.beagle.gz", sep = "\t",
       col.names = TRUE, row.names = FALSE)

phred <- beagle2pl("test_sub.beagle.gz")
res2 <- mechGEA(phred,
                patch_info = input_data$patch_info,
                patches_xy = input_data$patches_xy,
                migration_loci = 50,
                env = input_data$env,
                iter_sampling_gea = 100,
                iter_warmup_gea = 200,
                iter_sampling_mig = 100,
                iter_warmup_mig = 200)

# plot results
plot_manhattan(list(res, res2), list(beagle, "test_sub.beagle.gz"))
# Any combination of res/res$SNP_pvalues and filepaths/tables of metadata
# are allowed in lists. Assumes everything IS IN THE SAME ORDER!
} # }
